Primary={{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic|name=Catchmoon (Primary)}} |-|Secondary={{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic|name=Catchmoon (Secondary)}}
{{Quote|Secondary: Fires a wide-radius plasma energy projectile with a very short half-life.
Primary: Automatic trigger, faster fire rate and smaller projectiles.|In-game description}} '''Catchmoon''' is a [[Kitgun]] chamber component. It fires an energy projectile with [[Infinite Body Punch Through]], very similar to the {{Weapon|Arca Plasmor}}, while dealing {{D|Impact}} and {{D|Heat}} damage, as well as a guaranteed {{D|Impact}} proc against enemies within '''9''' meters. However, the projectile possesses [[Projectile Speed|travel time]], damage falloff, limited range, and no bonus damage on [[headshot]]s. The projectile will also dissipate if the center part of it collides with the environment. As a primary, it fires on full-auto with significantly smaller projectiles. As a secondary, it semi-automatically fires a wide projectile. ==Acquisition== The blueprint for the chamber can be bought from [[Rude Zuud]] for {{sc|500}} at Rank 0 with [[Solaris United]]. {{BuildRequire |buildcredits = 5,000 |build1 = Mytocardia Spore |build1amount = 15 |build2 = Travocyte Alloy |build2amount = 20 |build3 = Scrubber Exa Brain |build3amount = 10 |build4 = Alloy Plate |build4amount = 1,700 |buildtime = 1 |buildrush = 25 |blueprint = 500 |blueprintunit = Standing }} To craft the actual [[Kitgun]], players must have at least one built Catchmoon chamber, a chosen grip, and a chosen loader components. See [[Kitgun]] for more details. {{clr}} ==Stats== {{CustomCollapsible|Kitgun Build Table|||}} {{Transclude|Catchmoon/Table}} {{CustomCollapsible/End}} ==Notes== *All projectiles have travel time. ===Primary=== *Uses Shotgun mods. *Projectile lifetime is 0.42 second. Limited range of 42 meters. *Has linear damage falloff from 100% to 5.84% from 20m to 40m target distance (distances are affected by [[Projectile Speed]]). ===Secondary=== *Has linear damage falloff from 100% to 6.25% from 8m to 16m target distance (distances are affected by [[Projectile Speed]]). *Limited range of 20 meters. *Energy projectile from Catchmoon can ricochet from a certain surface; specifically, a platform where Warframe cryopod is located in Helene, [[Saturn]] and Hydron, [[Sedna]]. This also occurs on Corpus doors, which share a similar behavior with the Grineer defense platform, they are mobile 3D meshes. ==Tips== *{{M|Fatal Acceleration}}/{{M|Lethal Momentum}} is recommended to increase Catchmoon's limited range. **[[Projectile Speed]] mods also increase the distance at which enemies receive a forced {{D|Impact}} proc. *Although Catchmoon Kitguns do not deal increased damage on headshots, they can still trigger or receive benefits related to headshots such as {{A|Covenant}} or {{Arcane|Arcane Precision}}. ==Bugs== *Catchmoon Kitguns are not affected by the damage buff from {{A|Eclipse}}, but {{Arcane|Pax Seeker}}'s projectiles are affected normally. *{{M|Galvanized Savvy}} and {{M|Galvanized Shot}} are multiplicative to base damage sources on direct hits. ==Media== CatchmoonProjectile.png|Catchmoon projectile with default energy color. {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|KUep48GvsSk|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|6W6H4x2nvSQ|size=300px}} }} ==Patch Notes== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 15 Ammo per Pick Up: *Catchmoon (Primary) '''Secondary Weapon Ammo Pick up Overrides:''' 20 Ammo per Pick Up: *Catchmoon (Secondary) {{ver|30.6}} *Fixed Galvanized Mods not properly functioning with the Catchmoon’s guaranteed Impact proc. {{ver|29.5}} *Fixed inability to equip Skins on the Catchmoon Primary Kitgun {{ver|29.3.0.1}} *Increased accuracy and reduced recoil of the Primary Catchmoon Kitgun when used with Tremor and Steadyslam Grips. **''This change was planned for the upcoming Infested Kitguns but needed to squeak in early for the Riven Disposition changes!'' {{ver|28.0.5}} ;Primary Kitgun changes Below are balance changes that affect Primary Kitguns only based on feedback. ;Catchmoon *Projectile lifetime increased from 0.3secs to .42secs. *Fall Off increased from 12-24m to 20-40m. ;Brash Grip *Damage reduction lowered from -38 to -24 when used with Catchmoon Chamber. ;Shrewd Grip *Damage reduction lowered from -19 to -12 when used with Catchmoon Chamber. {{ver|26}} ;Catchmoon Changes: If you’ve made it to this part of the Update notes, you’re well aware that a lot of the Warframe meta may shift in new directions. With the current path Catchmoon weapons are on, it was time to bring Catchmoon weapons to a more reasonable power level, while still keeping them effective. *Decreased fall off damage from 100 to 10. *Decreased range of projectile from 40m to 20m and fall off range from 20-30m to 8-16m. {{ver|25.8}} *Catchmoon disposition changed from 0.6 to 0.5 {{ver|25.7.5}} *Fixed Catchmoon Kitguns not being able to damage the Ropalolyst Synovia. {{ver|25.0.3}} *Fixed an issue that made Catchmoon projectiles deal damage twice on the hit when the projectile is destroyed. This was not a case of ‘always worked this way’ as it was accidentally introduced by the Jovian Concord. {{ver|24.6}} *Catchmoon's projectile will now only collide with world geometry when the center of it hits. {{ver|24.4.4}} *Changed the following when Thunderdrum Loader is used with Catchmoon Chamber: **Critical Chance increased from 13% to 17% **Status Chance decreased from 35% to 28% }} ==See Also== *{{Weapon|Arca Plasmor}}, a Corpus shotgun that fires a similar projectile. *{{Weapon|Fulmin}}, a Tenno rifle that fires a similar projectile. {{KitgunNav}} [[de:Catchmoon]] [[es:Catchmoon]] [[Category:Update 24]] [[Category:Components]] [[Category:Kitgun]] [[uk:Спіймаймісяць]]

Primary={{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic|name=Gaze (Primary)}} |-|Secondary={{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic|name=Gaze (Secondary)}}
{{for|{{WF|Xaku}}'s ability|The Lost}} {{Quote|Secondary: a persistent cutting beam of pure energy.
Primary: same as Secondary, but with explosion on impact.|In-game description}} '''Gaze''' is a [[Kitgun]] chamber component. It fires a pinpoint-accurate [[Continuous Weapon|continuous beam]]. When used as a primary, the beam projects a 3 meter radial field at the point of impact, dealing pure {{D|Radiation}} damage. When used as a secondary, the beam has 1 meter of innate [[punch through]], can chain to an enemy within 5m (center-to-center, so actual range may seem shorter) of target and can chain to one additional enemy near the chained enemy for a total of 2 chained enemies, dealing {{D|Radiation}} and {{D|Puncture}} damage. ==Acquisition== The blueprint for the chamber can be bought from [[Rude Zuud]] for {{sc|500}} at Rank 0 with [[Solaris United]]. {{BuildRequire |buildcredits = 5,000 |build1 = Tepa Nodule |build1amount = 15 |build2 = Venerdo Alloy |build2amount = 40 |build3 = Kriller Thermal Laser |build3amount = 40 |build4 = Cryotic |build4amount = 1,200 |buildtime = 1 |buildrush = 25 |blueprint = 500 |blueprintunit = Standing }} To craft the actual [[Kitgun]], players must have at least one built Gaze chamber, a chosen grip, and a chosen loader components. See [[Kitgun]] for more details. {{clr}} ==Stats== {{CustomCollapsible|Kitgun Build Table|||}} {{Transclude|Gaze/Table}} {{CustomCollapsible/End}} ==Notes== ===Primary=== *Uses Rifle mods. *The zone of impact or maximum beam range creates a spherical area of effect of 3 meters, dealing the weapon's full damage. **[[Punch through]] affects the location of the weapon's area of effect. The weapon's area of effect is applied at the final point of contact rather than whenever an enemy is struck. **The area of effect radius can be increased with {{M|Firestorm}} ({{M|Primed Firestorm|Primed}}). **The radial damage is not affected by multishot. *Similarly to the Vermisplicer, the Grip chosen with the Gaze affects the '''range''' of the beam, and '''not''' the fire rate. Grips with higher damage output will reduce the range of the beam, while grips with lower damage will increase it. **When paired with the Tremor grip, the range of the beam is '''16 m'''. **When paired with the Steadyslam grip, the range of the beam is '''20 m'''. **When paired with the Shrewd grip, the range of the beam is '''26 m'''. **When paired with the Palmaris grip, the range of the beam is '''28 m'''. **When paired with the Brash grip, the range of the beam is '''30 m'''. *The range of the main beam can be increased with {{M|Sinister Reach}}. ===Secondary=== *The beam will chain to the closest living enemy with 5m on contact with an enemy. From there it will chain again, up to a maximum of 2 chains in total. A chain will do {{MathText|0.2{{exp|n}}}} times the main beams damage, where '''n''' is the chain number. *Similarly to the Vermisplicer, the Grip chosen with the Gaze affects the '''range''' of the beam, and '''not''' the fire rate. Grips with higher damage output will reduce the range of the beam, while grips with lower damage will increase it. **When paired with the Haymaker grip, the range of the beam is '''22 m'''. **When paired with the Lovetap grip, the range of the beam is '''25 m'''. **When paired with the Ulnaris grip, the range of the beam is '''30''' '''m'''. **When paired with the Ramble grip, the range of the beam is '''38 m'''. **When paired with the Gibber grip, the range of the beam is '''41 m'''. *The range of the main beam can be increased with {{M|Ruinous Extension}}. **However, it has no effect on the chain beam. *Has innate 1m [[Punch Through]]. ==Tips== *When continuously striking a surface or an enemy, the beam generates an excessive amount of particle effects, making it very difficult to discern where the beam is hitting, counterintuitive to the weapon's pinpoint accuracy. **To increase visibility, it is is advised to go into the game's options, and set the "GPU Particles" display setting to Medium, Low, or Disabled. **Changing the energy color of the weapon to a dark color, or black can also help. *{{M|Heavy Caliber}}/{{M|Magnum Force}}'s accuracy penalty are minimal on this weapon. ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 40 Ammo per Pick Up: *Gaze (Primary) '''Secondary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 20 Ammo per Pick Up: *Gaze (Secondary) '''Many weapons have also had their maximum ammo capacity adjusted.''' Primary Weapons: *Gaze (Primary): From 400 to 200 Secondary Weapons: *Gaze (Secondary): From 400 to 200 {{ver|29.5.6}} *Fixed force feedback not working properly with beam Kitguns. {{ver|28.0.5}} ;Primary Kitgun changes Below are balance changes that affect Primary Kitguns only based on feedback. ;Gaze *Range increased from 18m to 30m with Brash Grip. *Range increased from 15m to 26m with Shrewd Grip. *Range increased from 12m to 20 with Steadyslam Grip. *Range increased from 9m to 16 with Tremor Grip. {{ver|27.0.7}} *Fixed Kitguns with the 'Gaze' Chamber type and Pax Charge Arcane not recharging correctly. {{ver|25}} *The Gaze Kitgun Chamber now chains to up to two targets within 5m. }} {{KitgunNav}} [[de:Gaze]] [[es:Gaze]] [[Category:Update 24]] [[Category:Components]] [[Category:Kitgun]] [[uk:Вдива]] [[Category:Chaining Weapons]]

Primary={{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic|name=Tombfinger (Primary)}} |-|Secondary={{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic|name=Tombfinger (Secondary)}}
{{Quote|Secondary: fires projectiles semi-automatically with high accuracy; area-of-effect explosion on impact.
Primary: hold fire to charge for an even greater effect.|In-game description}} '''Tombfinger''' is a [[Kitgun]] chamber component. As a primary, it can be charged, with uncharged projectiles having a small explosion radius and fully charged projectiles having a significantly large explosion but without any {{D|Puncture}} damage. When used as a secondary, it fires a small, precise projectile that has [[Projectile Speed|travel time]] and detonates upon the first enemy or surface hit, dealing {{D|Impact}}, {{D|Puncture}} and {{D|Radiation}} damage with a guaranteed {{D|Impact}} proc. ==Acquisition== The blueprint for the chamber can be bought from [[Rude Zuud]] for {{sc|500}} at Rank 0 with [[Solaris United]]. {{BuildRequire |buildcredits = 5,000 |build1 = Thermal Sludge |build1amount = 15 |build2 = Axidrol Alloy |build2amount = 20 |build3 = Tink Dissipator Coil |build3amount = 10 |build4 = Circuits |build4amount = 900 |buildtime = 1 |buildrush = 25 |blueprint = 500 |blueprintunit = Standing }} To craft the actual [[Kitgun]], players must have at least one built Tombfinger chamber, a chosen grip, and a chosen loader components. See [[Kitgun]] for more details. {{clr}} ==Stats== {{CustomCollapsible|Kitgun Build Table|||}} {{Transclude|Tombfinger/Table}} {{CustomCollapsible/End}} ==Notes== ===Primary=== *Uses Rifle mods. *The Grip chosen with the Tombfinger affects the '''charge time''' in addition to the fire rate and damage. Grips with higher damage output will increase the charge time, while grips with lower damage will reduce it. **When paired with the Brash grip the charge time is '''0.5 s''', the quick shot AoE damage is 30 Radiation, and the charged shot AoE damage is 412 Radiation. **When paired with the Palmaris grip the charge time is '''0.5 s''', the quick shot AoE damage is 35 Radiation, and the charged shot AoE damage is 417 Radiation **When paired with the Shrewd grip, the charge time is '''0.8 s''', the quick shot AoE damage is 40 Radiation, and the charged shot AoE damage is 422 Radiation. **When paired with the Steadyslam grip, the charge time is '''1.1 s''', the quick shot AoE damage is 79 Radiation, and the charged shot AoE damage is 461 Radiation. **When paired with the Tremor grip, the charge time is '''1.4 s''', the quick shot AoE damage is 108 Radiation, and the charged shot AoE damage is 490 Radiation. *The weapon fires as soon as it has reached a full charge, which can lead to premature firing. *While charging significantly affects the explosion's characteristics, the only change to the projectile is damage distribution. *Quick shots have a base explosion radius of '''1.7''' meters, while fully charged shots have a base explosion radius of '''6.2''' meters. **Initial hit and explosion apply status separately. **All explosions inflicts [[Stagger|self-stagger]]. **All explosions have a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] multiplier of 1x and cannot trigger headshot conditions. **Explosion has linear [[Damage Falloff]] from: ***100% to 75% from central impact on uncharged shots. ***100% to 30% from central impact on fully charged shots. **All explosions can benefit from {{M|Firestorm}} ({{M|Primed Firestorm|Primed}}) and {{M|Cautious Shot}}. *Because Tombfinger's projectile has travel time, it is much less suitable to be built for the purpose of long range engagements, despite it being an accurate and powerful semi-auto chamber, with no damage falloff. **Hitting a target at range requires leading the target before firing. **Mods such as {{M|Terminal Velocity}} can help shots connect. ===Secondary=== *Upon impact, the projectile explodes in a '''1.9''' meter radius in a reverse-cone shape, dealing damage to enemies in front of the original target. **Initial hit and explosion apply status separately. **Explosion inflicts [[Stagger|self-stagger]]. **Explosion has a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] multiplier of 1x and cannot trigger headshot conditions. **Explosion has linear [[damage Falloff]] from 100% to 70% from central impact. **Can benefit from {{M|Fulmination}} ({{M|Primed Fulmination|Primed}}). *The {{D|Impact}}, {{D|Puncture}} and ~19.5% of the {{D|Radiation}} damage make up the direct hit, the remaining ~80.5% of Radiation damage is assigned to the explosion. **For example a kitgun built with Tombfinger with 180 base damage deals 91 is on direct hit and 89 with the splash. **The status chance remains the same for both the direct hit and the explosion. *Because Tombfinger's projectile has [[Projectile Speed|travel time]], it is much less suitable to be built for the purpose of long range engagements, despite it being an accurate and powerful semi-auto chamber, with no damage falloff. **Hitting a target at range requires leading the target before firing. **Mods such as {{M|Lethal Momentum}} can help shots connect. == Known Bugs == * {{M|Galvanized Aptitude}} and {{M|Galvanized Shot}} are multiplicative to base damage sources on direct hits. ==Trivia== *The Tombfinger Chamber was originally named the "Chillfinger" during [[TennoCon/2018|TennoCon 2018]]. ==Media== {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|ud8DDOM9QJY|size=300px}} }} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|35.1}} *Refined the volume of Tombfinger’s explosion sound effects. {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 20 Ammo per Pick Up: *Tombfinger (Primary) '''Secondary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 20 Ammo per Pick Up: *Tombfinger (Secondary) '''Many weapons have also had their maximum ammo capacity adjusted.''' Primary Weapons: *Tombfinger (Primary): From 540 to 120 ;Headshot Damage Changes During playtesting, the ammo changes alone weren’t enough to significantly change things for AoE weapons. So instead of tightening these values to be overly restrictive, we chose to address other factors that make these weapons so strong, such as headshot damage. Our approach here is two-fold, to reduce the impact of headshots for AOE weapons, but to also make precision headshots pack a larger punch overall. *Radial damage no longer gains extra headshot damage or triggers headshot conditions. **This is primarily targeted at the Ignis Wraith - as a “flamethrower” weapon, it’s hard to imagine a blanket of elements being precise enough to target weak points specifically. Explosive projectiles themselves can still land headshots, so there is still a reason to aim with most weapons for maximum damage. {{ver|28.0.5}} ;Primary Kitgun changes Below are balance changes that affect Primary Kitguns only based on feedback. ;Tombfinger *Charge time decreased from 0.8secs to 0.5secs with Brash Grip. *Charge time increased from 0.8secs to 1.1secs with Steadyslam Grip. *Charge time increased from 0.8secs to 1.4secs with Tremor Grip. ;Brash Grip *Damage reduction lowered from -28 to -20 when used with Tombfinger Chamber. ;Shrewd Grip *Damage reduction lowered from -14 to -10 when used with Tombfinger Chamber. {{ver|28.0.3}} *Terminal Velocity can now be used with Primary Tombfinger Kitguns. {{ver|27.3}} *Fixed Radial Attack Mods not having any effect on Tombfinger Kitguns. {{ver|27.2}}
Reduced the following AoE weapons Radial Damage Falloff from central impact that were all previously 90%: *Tombfinger: 30% ;Self Damage Changes : We are getting rid of Self Damage and replacing it with something else: instead of Self Damage, it’s now ‘Stagger’. This change completely removes the chance of killing yourself, and instead now creates scenarios where you will interrupt yourself - or ‘Stagger’ - to varying degrees if you aren’t careful. The degrees of Self-Interrupt start with a small stumble all the way to full knockdown depending on how close you are to the center of explosion. Any Mods referring to Self Damage will be converted to acknowledge Stagger. With this Self-Interrupt system, we have added dozens of new recovery animations that harness a ninja-like recovery experience. By pressing ‘Jump’ at the correct time, you can execute a ninja-skill-based knockdown recovery to ALL in-game knockdowns. This ninja recovery window is indicated by a glowing FX on your Warframe. In addition to Self Damage being removed, some of the more powerful AOE weapons without Self Damage presently will have the Stagger added, but it should only be noticeable in cases of extreme inaccuracy on the player’s part. The Weapons include: *Tombfinger In the original Dev Workshop, we said:
''As a result of this overall systemic change, Weapons with Stagger will be getting approximately a 20% buff in Damage, with any weapons with AOE receiving a 50% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact.'' This is no longer accurate after continued testing. What we are doing now is: No damage buffs have been added, but any weapons with AOE are receiving ~20% increase in Radius. Additionally, AOE weapons are receiving a 90% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact. This means on the very outer section of the explosion Radius 10% of the Damage will be dealt. Tactics will be deadly - aim true, Tenno. ''Why: Several players brought up the history of the Tonkor and we want to make sure we ship this change in a place that’s conservative in its starting point from a balance perspective. The complete removal of Self Damage does change the pace of destruction with some of the game’s most powerful weapons, so we want to make sure we can iterate upwardly instead of releasing a bonanza of explosions with no other choices.'' }} {{KitgunNav}} [[de:Tombfinger]] [[es:Tombfinger]] [[Category:Update 24]] [[Category:Components]] [[Category:Kitgun]] [[Category:Self Interrupt Weapons]] [[uk:Бецман]]

{{ArcaneBox}}
'''Pax Bolt''' is an [[Arcane Enhancement]] for a [[Kitgun]] that increases [[Ability Strength]] and [[Ability Efficiency]] for the next ability after a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] kill.

==Effect==
{| class="emodtable"
|-
! Rank !! Ability Strength & Efficiency
|-
| 0 || 7.5%
|-
| 1 || 15%
|-
| 2 || 22.5%
|-
| 3 || 30%
|}

==Acquisition==
Can be bought from [[Rude Zuud]] for {{sc|10,000}} per arcane upon reaching the rank of '''Old Mate'''.

==Notes==
*[[:Category:Channeled Abilities|Channeled Abilities]] (e.g., {{A|Exalted Blade}}, {{A|Renewal}}) that are activated during the Pax Bolt buff will keep the [[Ability Strength]] bonus on them for as long as they are kept active, even after Pax Bolt has expired.
**This does '''not''' apply to the [[Ability Efficiency]] part of the buff. The bonus Ability Efficiency will be removed and updated the moment that Pax Bolt expires.
**Subsequent Pax Bolt buffs will temporarily reduce the energy drain for any currently active channeled abilities for the duration of Pax Bolt. Whether this is intentional or not is unknown.
*Similar to other [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] kill conditions, the enemy must be killed by a headshot through weapon damage, and not any damage-over-time [[Status|status effect]] such as {{D|Slash}}.
*The Ability Strength and [[Ability Efficiency]] gained are '''additive''' with other mods. For example, a Warframe equipped with maxed {{M|Intensify}} and receives a Rank 3 Pax Bolt buff would have +60% Ability Strength.
*Note that [[Ability Efficiency]] still caps out at 175% even with Pax Bolt equipped, though channeled abilities use uncapped values.
*Works oddly with Wisp's [[Reservoirs]]; the bonus strength will apply, but if the player already has a weaker mote active, touching the new buffed mote will simply refresh it rather than change its strength. In order to take full advantage of Pax Bolt, you must wait for your current buffs to expire.

==Trivia==
*Inscription on Pax Bolt is [[Solaris Language]], reading "BAWLT" forming the sound "Bolt".

==Patch History==
{{Scrollbox/Article|
{{ver|31.6}}
;ARCANE STAT CHANGES PER RANK

We’ve adjusted the values of older Arcanes with the goal of making lower rank Arcanes more viable, and more desirable while collecting as a result. In short, there are three stats that each Arcane tends to have (speaking generally) -- for example, a percentage chance, a stat buff, and the duration of the buff. 

Certain Arcanes increase all of these stats per rank (making them scale exponentially), but we are changing it so that only one stat is affected by rank (making it scale linearly). The other stats will now be at the max-rank value regardless of the Arcane Rank, thereby buffing lower-rank Arcanes as a result.

;Pax Bolt 
On Headshot Kill: 100% (was 25%) chance for +7.5%/30% Ability Efficiency and +7.5%/30% Ability Strength on the next Ability used within 4s (was 1s)
*Now that the chance is guaranteed, the new description is “On Headshot Kill: +7.5%/30% Ability Efficiency and +7.5%/30% Ability Strength on the next Ability used within 4s”

{{ver|28.2.1}}
*Fixed Pax Bolt not triggering on equipped Primary Kitguns.

{{ver|28.1}}
*Fixed Pax Bolt being able to be activated by weapons/abilities other than the Kitgun it's installed on (sometimes resulting in a script error).

{{ver|24}}
*Introduced.
}}

{{ArcaneBox}}
'''Pax Charge''' is an [[Arcane Enhancement]] for [[Kitgun]]s that changes the Magazine type to a [[Reload#Rechargeable weapons|rechargeable battery]], like that of the {{Weapon|Cycron}}. Each rank of the enhancement reduces the recharge delay before ammo can regenerate.

==Effect==
{| class="emodtable"
|-
! Rank !! Recharge Delay
|-
| 0 || 12.5%
|-
| 1 || 25%
|-
| 2 || 37.5%
|-
| 3 || 50%
|}

==Acquisition==
Can be bought from [[Rude Zuud]] for {{sc|10,000}} per arcane upon reaching the rank of '''Old Mate'''.

==Notes==
*Recharge rate is '''not''' affected by mods or abilities. Recharge rate depends on the chamber part:
{| class="wikitable"
|+ Recharge Rate
|-
! colspan=1 | Chamber
| Primary || Secondary
|-
! {{Weapon|Catchmoon|Catchmoon}}
| 5 ammo/sec || 50 ammo/sec
|-
! {{Weapon|Gaze|Gaze}}
| 50 ammo/sec || 50 ammo/sec
|-
! {{Weapon|Rattleguts|Rattleguts}}
| 50 ammo/sec || 50 ammo/sec
|-
! {{Weapon|Sporelacer|Sporelacer}}
| 5 ammo/sec || 25 ammo/sec
|-
! {{Weapon|Tombfinger|Tombfinger}}
| 50 ammo/sec || 50 ammo/sec
|-
! {{Weapon|Vermisplicer|Vermisplicer}}
| 50 ammo/sec || 25 ammo/sec
|-
|}
*Similar to [[Archgun]]s and the {{Weapon|Cycron}}, base recharge delay is equal to the reload time displayed on the weapon.
**Reduced reload time (recharge delay) is shown in the [[Arsenal]] upon equipping Pax Charge.
**Recharge delay is further reduced (stacking additively) by reload speed mods like {{M|Quickdraw}} and {{M|Stunning Speed}}.
*Reduces the recharge delay by increasing reload speed. At max rank, it increases the reload speed by 50%, which reduces the recharge delay by 33.3%. See [[Reload Speed]] for the details.
**For example, with a Kitgun that has a reload time of 2.1 seconds:
***Unranked Pax Charge will result in a recharge delay of <math>{
\frac{2.1}{1 + 12.5\%} = 1.87
}</math> seconds, a reduction of 11.1%.
***Rank 3 Pax Charge will result in a recharge delay of <math>{
\frac{2.1}{1 + 50\%} = 1.4
}</math> seconds, a reduction of 33.3%.
*Prevents the weapon from receiving benefit from reload-triggered mods or Arcanes such as {{M|Pressurized Magazine}} or {{Arcane|Arcane Awakening}}.

==Tips==
*Pax Charge is useful for prolonged missions due to never requiring actual ammunition, however this also means you are limited to essentially your original magazine size of ammo before having to recharge.
**[[Carrier]] sentinel, equipped with {{M|Ammo Case}}, is an alternative to keep ammo reserves up in missions, although this requires picking up of ammo and the sentinel to be alive.
**{{M|Pistol Ammo Mutation}} ({{M|Primed Pistol Ammo Mutation|Primed}}) or {{M|Pistol Scavenger}} can be used as alternative as well, at a cost of a mod slot and capacity in a Kitgun or an aura slot in a Warframe, respectively.
*Pax Charge can be used in conjunction with {{M|Synth Charge}} to reload only the last shot in the magazine, however it will often reload multiple shots before the player is able to fire them with semi-auto kitguns.
*A Kitgun equipped with Pax Charge will almost always require a longer time to fully recharge the magazine than the actual normal reload of the weapon.
**The Sporelacer and Catchmoon secondaries, as well as both Tombfinger variants, can recharge faster than the game will automatically reload your weapon. However, there is a [[Reload#Manual Reload|delay]] before the automatic reload starts that can be circumvented by manually reloading, which cannot be performed while using Pax Charge. While this can be circumvented with enough fire rate, it may be impractical to fire the weapons fast enough given their semi-automatic trigger type.
*Recharge delay can be reduced by abilities that affect reload speed, but recharge rate will '''not''' be affected. Recharge delay is affected by:
**{{WF|Chroma}}'s {{A|Elemental Ward}} with {{D|Toxin}} alignment
**{{WF|Volt}}'s {{A|Speed}}
**{{WF|Harrow}}'s {{A|Penance}}
**{{WF|Gauss}}'s {{A|Redline}}
